seal.statement: In the failing formation traced in the second causal packet of 2026-09-19, a joiner's planning owner serves a deferred readiness snapshot of the seed for 173 s - every dimension false, the previous reasons inherited, the old observedAt carried over - routing denies on it without regard to its age, and the heartbeat write it filters lets the node's ready lease lapse. Which condition keeps a new build from being admitted cannot be observed: every term of the planning owner's reuse decision and every refusal of its publish decision is silent, the routing denial does not say how old the record it trusted is or that it was deferred, and the caller of a query whose every candidate was filtered by readiness receives the same error as for a partition service that does not exist. This quest makes those observable without changing them. The planning owner logs, per owner key, each transition between serving an admitted record and serving a deferred one and each change of the failing terms while deferred, naming the terms of the reuse decision that failed from the one evaluation that decided, the age of the record whose verdict is being inherited, and on return to an admitted record the time spent deferred; a refused publish is logged with its refusal reason under the same once-per-change rule. The routing denial line states, for each denied candidate it already lists, the age of the readiness record the denial was made on and whether that record was deferred. The error returned when every candidate was filtered by readiness carries a machine-readable cause that distinguishes it from a missing partition service. No decision, schedule, retry cadence, error message, error code, log message text or existing log field changes.

text: Named the planning owner's admission and publication terms without moving a decision. New owner module src/control-plane/readiness-admission-transition-record.js keeps one per-owner-key record in a WeakMap keyed by the planning owner: the read hot path compares one integer signature (deferred bit plus the failed-term bit set), counts suppressed repeats, and only a change allocates, reads the owner clock or logs. canReuseCompletedSnapshot is now evaluateCompletedSnapshotReuse returning that bit set, with the same order and the same short-circuit; readSync wraps each of its five returns in noteAdmissionRead, which hands the served snapshot straight back and states deferred from the deferred snapshot's own readinessPlanningTokenStatus. captureCompletionCurrency states the five completion-currency terms and reports a refused publish once per change of reason. isDeferredReadinessPlanningSnapshot moved to its marker's owner (readiness-planning-version-contract) and control-plane-mutation-readiness now consumes it instead of restating it; eligibility-snapshot owns resolveReadinessObservedAgeMs. The routing denial entry gains observedAgeMs (from the executor's own nowFn, null when it has none) and deferred, and the partition failure result gains routingDenialCause from the routing snapshot's typed reason code. No message, code, schedule, budget, retry or existing log field changed.

Reachability of the named terms, measured on the real owner. Driven and asserted: live_evidence_veto, transport_topology_invalid (through the readSync barrier), planning_identity_saturated, freshness_not_current, generation_saturated; on the publish side planning_identity_not_current, completion_token_not_current and transport_topology_invalid. Exercised but not asserted: completed_record_absent (the cold read takes the bootstrap path and is served admitted). NOT driven, so named and wired but never observed to fire: source_change_unclassified on either path, and publication_guard_changed. Found unreachable from readSync: build_options_key_changed - readCompleted is keyed by buildOptionsKey, so completed.buildOptionsKey === buildOptionsKey always holds there, and handleStaleCompletion's legacy call passes the record it just built; the term is kept because canReuseCompletedSnapshot still states it, but no input reaches it. This is a finding for the planning owner, not a repair this quest makes (R17).

Measured decision-neutrality and hot-path cost. The frozen oracle digest e1939d2d3963bd9f4cdd6a36ec9a21d9db05701e0d134a0eaed116c9086eecba and the denial-payload digest 42fe86ce6fdbe70b03c7fa501c9f457e16af5c03e1da539426e438df6d891e44 were each measured twice: once on the tree at b869139a6 with no source line of this quest applied, and once after, with the same rig file - both identical. Owner call counts over the same scenario are identical on both trees (readPlanningProjectionIdentity 76, captureToken 58, readCurrentSourceObservation 169, hasUnclassifiedSourceChange 240, isCompletedSnapshotLive 17, capturePositiveDecisionLiveVeto 30, capturePublicationGuard 26, captureCurrentPlanningSource 53, readCompleted 41, readSync 28). Over 200 reads in an unchanged admitted state both trees read the owner clock 3 times per read and emit zero lines, so the transition detector adds no clock read, no allocation and no emission in the steady state.

round 1 REJECT (7 blocking; no changed decision found - two differentials against main, 288000 + 49740 ops, 0 divergences). B1 transition-bounded: recorder state is keyed by ownerKey only while the owner's state is per (ownerKey, buildOptionsKey); one key read as planning (deferred) and routed (bridged, admitted) logs on EVERY read - 1000 reads, 999 lines, suppressed 0; the traced 173 s freeze shape gives 1695 lines/min on node-0 and the lines describe a flap that is not happening. B2 statement clause 'the error returned carries a machine-readable cause': routingDenialCause lives only on executeOnPartition's internal result and is dropped by both buildParticipantFailureEntry copies, executeInsert's Error, the sql-query-engine transaction throws and partition-split-routing; the caller of a frozen write still sees DISTRIBUTED_PARTICIPANT_FAILURE / 'Partition service not found' with no cause; the receipt asserts only the raw internal value. B3 the cause is never reset: filtered first, admitted during the retry wait, delivery then fails -> 'participant offline' with routingDenialCause all_services_filtered_by_readiness. B4 beyond 64 owner keys FIFO eviction restarts records from unobserved: 66 deferred keys, 1320 steady reads, 1320 lines. B5 decision-neutral: main's planning owner has no logger use; an unguarded logger.info inside readSync and captureCompletionCurrency makes a throwing logger fail reads and abort a refused publish (retryableBuildFailureCount 1 vs 0, buildCount 3 vs 4), and the throw precedes the record update so the next read emits again. B6 suppressedRefusals untruthful: a successful publish resets the signature and discards the count (six refusals, one line, publish, next refusal says suppressed 0). B7 proof regression: readiness-planning-deferral-bounded spies on canReuseCompletedSnapshot, which readSync no longer calls; the audit observes 577 serves against main's 646 - all 69 missing are read-path admissions - and stays green. Non-blocking: the decisions-unchanged receipt does not kill a publish-guard-dropped mutant (D3); 12 of 34 mutations survive incl. four mislabelled terms and a dead withheld branch (cap 8 = term count); the untested terms are correct when driven and should be pinned; build_options_key_changed unreachability confirmed in code; extra owner-clock reads (recorder once per transition incl. the silent first admission; executor nowFn + Date.parse per denied node per routing snapshot, not covered by the log throttle); routingDenialCause leaks into the CDC authoritative read result through a spread; observedAgeMs negative for a future-dated stamp. Statics all green with the work staged; 38 related suites green.

Round-1 verifier repair, seven blocking findings. B1/N5: the transition record is keyed by the identity the owner keys its served state by - owner key, build-options key AND participation kind, because only a ROUTED_READ may take the sealed CL-012 bridge - and all three are on the line; the round-1 repro falls from 999 lines in 1000 reads to 1, and the traced 'freeze' log-volume shape from 4892 lines in 25950 reads to 14. B4: the private 64-key FIFO is gone; the recorder forgets a variant exactly where rememberBuildOptions discards one and drops everything on shutdown, so its size is the owner's own bounded per-owner variant state (66 keys over 1320 steady reads: 1320 lines -> 0; pinned at 200 keys and at the owner's 16-variant cap). B5: emission is the last thing that happens and is caught; the record is advanced before it; a refused emission is counted and the count rides the next line that gets out, and never appears in getDiagnostics - a throwing logger now gives main's reads, publishes and build count exactly. B6: the publish record is a two-state machine like the read side, so refused->published is a line stating suppressedRefusals and refusedForMs. B3: routingDenialCause is reset the moment a resolution finds candidates, so a delivery failure no longer carries a stale readiness cause. B2: the cause travels as an additive own field on both participant-failure entry builders, the coordinator's own projection and failure outcome, the Error executeInsert throws, the four sql-query-engine transaction throws and routeSplitMirroredWrite - message, code, class and result shape unchanged on SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and a transaction, for both the filtered and the missing-service cause. B7: readSync reaches the decision through canReuseCompletedSnapshot again, so the deferral-bounded audit observes 646 serves as it does on main, and that count is now sealed in that test. N4: the recorder reads no clock at all - it takes the observation time the caller already read - and the executor computes observedAgeMs only where the throttled denial line is built. Oracles re-measured on b869139a6 with the final rig: scenario digest, ticking-clock digest, both denial-payload digests and all eleven owner call counts are identical.

Blast radius of the routing denial cause, and two places it deliberately does not go. It reaches a CLIENT on one surface: src/admin/admin-query-result-message-envelope.js forwards participant-failure entries verbatim (slice to PARTICIPANT_FAILURES_LIMIT) into the admin query-result message, which is what the admin websocket sends, so an operator - and the demo driver - can read it. It also rides the CDC authoritative-read result through the ...result spread in src/cdc/cdc-integration-service-owner-rpc-read-execution.js normalizeAuthoritativeQueryRowSet; a test pins that no file under src/cdc mentions the field, so nothing there branches on it. It is NOT carried by src/query/distributed/distributed-write-coordinator.js, which re-projects participant failures into its own explicit field list (line 251) and drops it: a distributed multi-partition WRITE therefore still cannot name the cause. That surface was not in the lead's list and is left alone rather than widened (R16/R17); it is a finding for the query owner. Nothing reaches the PostgreSQL wire: src/query/pg/postgres-wire-adapter.js builds its error responses from a message string and never from the participant-failure entries. Also recorded: the heartbeat failure path does NOT already carry participant failures - heartbeat-service-publication-methods.js recordFailure(stage, errorMessage) is given only an Error's .message by its callers - so per the lead's condition the cause was not added there.

Mutation coverage after the repair, measured with a matrix re-expressed against the repaired source (41 mutants; the verifier's round-1 matrix could apply only 30 of its 34 to it, and 11 of its rows silently reported 'pattern matched 0 times'). 40 of 41 die with a NAMED failing test. One survives and is an equivalent mutant: T1, mislabelling the transport term inside collectCheapReuseTermFailures, because that term is unreachable from a read - readSync's ordered classification barrier returns before canReuseCompletedSnapshot is ever called with an invalid-transport token. Verified by hand, not inferred: the mutation applied, all eight owner witnesses passed. The sibling unreachable term build_options_key_changed is documented in the code with its reason and has no test. A second measurement trap worth recording: spawnSync's default 1 MB maxBuffer truncates the owner witness's reconcile trace and makes the runner report a failure that no test produced, which reads as a kill that never happened - it produced 7 false kills in the first run of my own matrix and 6 in the verifier's.

Process trap found while repairing: solve start writes sealedAt into the WORKING quest.json, but the red-on-revert dance stages the tree BEFORE sealing and later restores it with git checkout-index, which puts back the pre-seal copy and silently drops sealedAt. It was missing here for the whole of round 1 and the round-1 verifier did not catch it, because the probe reads the seal from log.ndjson and still measures. Restored from the log's own seal entry after checking the statement and doneWhen in quest.json are byte-identical to the sealed ones (they are); nothing sealed was reworded. Anyone using the sanctioned stage-revert-seal-restore sequence has to re-stage between solve start and the restore, or re-add sealedAt afterwards.

Scope decision (lead, attempt 3): the heartbeat failure line and the heartbeat's own failure record now state the routing denial cause. This goes beyond the sealed statement's literal error-cause clause, which names the error returned to a query caller, and is inside its stated purpose. It follows the owner's direction of 2026-09-19 (evening) recorded in the epic: make sure the repaired result preserves the actual freeze/refusal cause through the places where it is currently dropped - 'Partition service not found' is not sufficient if readiness admission is the responsible owner. The traced victim's heartbeat write to nodes-p1 failed with DISTRIBUTED_PARTICIPANT_FAILURE while every candidate was filtered by controlPlaneRecoveryEligible readiness, and recordFailure kept only the Error's .message, so the run's 'Heartbeat failing repeatedly' and register-stage lines read exactly like a partition with no service rows. recordFailure gains an optional third parameter (the caught error), one additive log field and one additive field on heartbeatPublicationDiagnostics, with a named absent value; no message text, no existing field and no branch moves, and a mutant that makes the escalation read the new field dies on the heartbeat differential.

Attempt 3, lead's close-the-gap directive. (1) Census of every site in src/query that rebuilds a participant or partition failure entry into an explicit field list, and the cause carried through each: query-execution-budget buildParticipantFailureEntry and buildPartitionExecutionFailureResult, query-executor-shared buildParticipantFailureEntry, parallel-query-partition-outcomes normalizePartitionExecutionFailureSnapshot and buildPartitionExecutionFailureOutcome, query-executor-partition-delivery's buildFailureResult closure - and the three the census found that round 2 missed: distributed-write-coordinator's participant-failure map, its log context and its throwing-participant projection, plus parallel-query-execution-metrics PartitionQueryMetrics.fail and formatQueryExecutionMetrics. The write coordinator now reads the cause through readRoutingDenialCause, the new counterpart of attachRoutingDenialCause, because a distributed result reports it on its participant failures rather than on itself. A test walks src/query for every file writing the distinctive participantAddress key and fails if one of them does not mention the cause, and pins the exact file set. (2) End-to-end witness of the traced victim's own path with real owners: the readiness-filtered rig executor runs the UPDATE, the real CDC buildSystemTableMutationError turns the failed result into the thrown Error, and the REAL HeartbeatService.start loop catches it at its register stage. The caught error's participant failure carries all_services_filtered_by_readiness, the missing-service case carries no_service_rows, and the message, code and class are main's. (3) recordFailure takes the caught error as an optional third argument and states the cause on the heartbeat failure line and on heartbeatPublicationDiagnostics, with a named 'unstated' absent value; no message text, no existing field and no branch changed, and the decisions-unchanged receipt now carries a heartbeat failure-path differential over a scripted five-error sequence whose digest equals main's. (4) The PostgreSQL wire adapter is pinned to build errors from message strings only. All five oracles and all eleven owner call counts re-measured on b869139a6 and identical.

Census of every site in src/query that rebuilds a participant or partition failure entry into an explicit field list, with the cause's status at each (attempt 3). CARRIES: (1) query-execution-budget buildParticipantFailureEntry; (2) query-execution-budget buildPartitionExecutionFailureResult, the field's origin; (3) query-executor-shared buildParticipantFailureEntry, a true duplicate of (1), kept as one by this quest; (4) parallel-query-partition-outcomes normalizePartitionExecutionFailureSnapshot; (5) parallel-query-partition-outcomes buildPartitionExecutionFailureOutcome; (6) distributed-write-coordinator's failed-participant map; (7) distributed-write-coordinator buildParticipantFailureLogContext; (8) distributed-write-coordinator executePartitionStatement's catch projection, for a participant whose statement THROWS; (9) parallel-query-execution-metrics PartitionQueryMetrics.fail; (10) parallel-query-execution-metrics formatQueryExecutionMetrics. NOT A RE-PROJECTION, so unchanged: query-executor-partition-delivery's buildFailureResult closure is where the field is set, not copied; query-executor-partition-failure buildQueryPartitionCandidateFailureDetails builds the DETAILS of a delivered-candidate failure and the cause rides the closure beside it; control-plane-system-table-gateway normalizeMutationResult and cdc buildSystemTableMutationError both spread rather than list fields, so they preserve it; query-executor-write-retry-routing and query-executor-partition-candidate-state build repair-request option bags, not failure entries. Sites 6-10 were found by this census and were dropping the cause after attempt 2. A test now walks src/query for every file writing the distinctive participantAddress object key, fails if one does not mention the field, and pins the exact six-file set.

Two pre-existing tests assert the exact shape of a payload this quest adds one field to, and were extended rather than weakened. test/control-plane/heartbeat-memory-trend.test.js deep-compares getHeartbeatPublicationDiagnostics() after a successful reporter heartbeat; it now expects lastFailureRoutingDenialCause: 'unstated', which is what a record with no failure in it says. test/query/distributed-write-coordinator-participant-failure-log.test.js deep-compares the participant entries on the coordinator's warn line; it now expects routingDenialCause: null for a failure that did not come out of a routing denial. Both keep their exact-shape assertions, so a third field would still fail them. Twenty-three further suites that touch participantFailures, the heartbeat, the gateway, the CDC write path, the admin envelope or the parallel coordinator were run one at a time and needed no change.

round 2 REJECT (2 blocking residuals; no changed decision - owner differential 6 configurations x 60 seeds x 800 ops, ticking-clock 20 seeds, production differential 40 x 1500 ops and a heartbeat-loop differential against a frozen archive of the seal, all 0 divergences). The cause SURVIVES the victim's own path end to end on real production owners (HeartbeatService.start -> sendHeartbeat -> system-table gateway -> CDC updateSystemTableRow -> engine executeQuery -> DistributedWriteCoordinator -> executeOnPartition -> routing filtered on controlPlaneRecoveryEligible): the denial is local to the joiner's own executor (0 messages delivered; no inter-node hop carries participant failures), the register catch site receives message, code and class identical to main's with participantFailures[0].routingDenialCause all_services_filtered_by_readiness (no_service_rows for the missing case), five consecutive beats incl. the repeated-failure warn lines carry it, and INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT and the gateway's upsert, insert and delete at critical class all carry it. B2-residual: SQLQueryEngine.buildCaughtQueryExecutionFailure (src/query/sql-query-engine.js ~637) turns a thrown Error into a result through an explicit field list that omits the cause, so for any statement inside a transaction the caller of executeQuery still receives 'Partition service not found' with no cause, identical for the filtered and the missing case; the census cannot see the site (no participantAddress key) and the transaction test calls deliverTransactionOperation on a bare prototype. B5-residual: resolveLogger(owner) sits outside the try in emit, so a throwing info getter, a throwing service.logger getter and a Proxy logger make 6 of 7 reads throw where main returns (build count 7 against 8). Closed: B1 (key complete: readSync is the only serving path; 400 reads, 1 line), B3, B4 (200 keys, 1600 steady reads, 0 lines; tracked count bounded by variants x kinds; 0 after shutdown), B6 (refusedForMs measures from the first refusal of the run: six refusals 1 s apart then a publish give 6000 and suppressed 5), B7 (main's unmodified audit bound to the subject observes 646 serves). Nothing branches on the heartbeat field and every consumer of heartbeatPublicationDiagnostics picks fields by name; the PostgreSQL wire never touches participant entries; no production consumer deep-compares the two extended payloads. 50 mutants at a 512 MB buffer: 48 killed; T1 confirmed equivalent by an identical digest of 9898 emitted lines; R8 (refusedSince reset on every refusal) survives. Non-blocking: the cause also dies at buildControlPlaneMutationDeferredFailure for non-critical writes (becomes query_admission_deferred; identical on main) and, from code reading, at the admin repair-failure summary's normalizeFirstFailedParticipant outside the census's walk; 17 build variants against the owner's cap of 16 log on every read (each a real owner state change); quiet volume about 69 lines per minute per node, all genuine transitions; an async rejecting sink leaves unhandled rejections. 62 of 62 related suites green; statics green.

Altitude check before a fourth attempt. Three attempts, two rejections, no decision ever changed: the rejections were all in the observables, and they came from breadth, not from a wrong idea. The quest spans three surfaces - the planning owner's transition recorder, the routing denial line, and the error cause - and the third turned out to be a propagation problem across many layers: a failure result is re-projected through explicit field lists at each layer (two duplicate participant-entry builders, the parallel-query outcome projections, the write coordinator's three, the metrics pair, the engine's caught-error projection), so an additive field dies wherever a list was not extended. That is a structural fact about the query path - a failure entry has no single constructor - and the durable cure is one owner of the failure-entry shape, which is a refactor outside an observability quest and is recorded here as a finding for the query owner, not attempted. For THIS quest the right altitude is unchanged and the remaining work is bounded: the verifier has now run the victim's real path end to end and the cause survives it; what is left is one more projection site (the engine's caught-error result, which hides the cause for transactional statements), a census keyed on how failure results are CONSTRUCTED rather than on one property name, the logger resolution moved inside its guard, and one pin. Splitting the quest now would strand verified work on two surfaces behind the third; proceeding with one bounded attempt is the smaller risk. If that attempt is rejected on the error-cause surface again, the error-cause clause is split into its own quest and the recorder and routing surfaces land without it.

The census that pins every failure-result constructor in the query tree is enumerated by CONSTRUCTION SHAPE, not by name. The test (test/query/readiness-routing-denial-observability.test.js, 'every failure-result constructor in the query tree carries the cause') walks every .js file under src/query plus the engine file, brace-matches each function body from its declaration line, and admits a body as a failure constructor when it (a) reads a failure off something it was handed (a result/error/entry/failure/metric/snapshot/errorLike/details property read, or the PROJECTION_READ regex), (b) mentions at least four of fourteen failure-shape keys, and (c) either sets success:false or mentions partitionId with at least five keys. Control-flow keywords are excluded so a guarded block is never mistaken for a constructor. The set is pinned exactly at nine entries, so a NEW constructor fails the test as an unpinned site and a constructor that stops carrying the cause fails it as a dropping site. What the method would still miss: (1) a failure shape built outside src/query - the control-plane, rebalancer, cdc and admin trees re-project participant failures and are covered by hand-written pins, not by this scan; (2) a constructor built incrementally across more than one function, since the scan is function-scoped; (3) a constructor naming fewer than four of the fourteen keys, e.g. one returning only {success:false, error}; (4) a re-projection performed by a generic copy (spread, structuredClone, JSON round-trip), which needs no change to carry the field and so is invisible to a scan looking for explicit key lists. The method found two sites that the earlier name-based and literal-based scans both missed: buildCaughtQueryExecutionFailure (sql-query-engine.js) and buildPartitionCallbackReadFailureResult (sql-query-engine-lifecycle-and-callback-dispatch.js).

RECORDED, NOT ACTED ON: the non-critical control-plane write loses its cause one layer above this quest's reach. buildControlPlaneMutationDeferredFailure (src/control-plane/control-plane-mutation-readiness.js:492) is the single builder behind both buildLocalControlPlaneMutationReadinessFailure and buildSystemTableMutationRoutingGapFailure. It projects the blocker into an explicit shape - reasonCodes, failedDimensions, runtimeAuthority, dependencyStates, retryAfterMs, errorCode, an owner contract outcome and a frozen details object whose only free-text field is details.cause = options.error.message. A non-critical write that is refused by mutation readiness therefore surfaces as query_admission_deferred carrying the readiness blocker's reason codes, and NOT carrying the routing denial cause this quest threads through the query tree: the two vocabularies are disjoint and the readiness blocker is a different owner's verdict than the routing resolution's. This is IDENTICAL on main - the layer never had the routing cause to lose - so it is a pre-existing gap, not a regression, and closing it would mean deciding which of two owners' verdicts a deferred control-plane write should name, which is an owner-boundary decision and outside an observability quest. Whoever picks this up should start by deciding whether details.cause is the right carrier or whether the deferred failure needs a second, typed field.

STRUCTURAL FINDING, RECORDED NOT CURED: a participant failure entry has no single constructor on the query path, so carrying one new field cost nine edits instead of one. The shape is built by two duplicate builders that must not be merged while their callers differ (buildParticipantFailureEntry in src/query/query-execution-budget.js and the copy in src/query/query-executor-shared.js), and is then RE-PROJECTED through explicit key lists at every layer that hands it on: parallel-query-execution-metrics.js (formatQueryExecutionMetrics and PartitionQueryMetrics.fail), parallel-query-partition-outcomes.js (two builders), distributed-write-coordinator.js (three sites), sql-query-engine.js (buildCaughtQueryExecutionFailure), sql-query-engine-lifecycle-and-callback-dispatch.js (buildPartitionCallbackReadFailureResult), and outside src/query the admin repair normalizer (normalizeFirstFailedParticipant). Each re-projection is a place a field can be silently dropped, and the census test this quest pins exists only because no type or single owner makes that impossible. The durable cure is one owner of the failure-entry shape - one module that constructs it, one that widens it, and pass-through (spread) everywhere else - which would make the census test unnecessary. That is a query-owner refactor with a real blast radius (every consumer that matches on the current explicit key set), and is deliberately NOT attempted here: this quest may not change a decision, and consolidating two builders whose callers differ would.

ADMIN SITE DECISION: normalizeFirstFailedParticipant (src/admin/admin-service-discovery-authoritative-repair-failures.js:58) now carries routingDenialCause, because the carry is a pure additive pass-through. Checked before acting: (1) src/diagnostics/control-plane-quiescence-snapshot.js never reads firstFailedParticipant at all - its only participant reference is the literal 'participant failure' in its own vocabulary - so the quiescence snapshot cannot move; (2) the classifier the admin summary decides with (src/control-plane/control-plane-error-classification.js) reads a FIXED field set - message, error, code, errorCode, deferRetry, retryAfterMs - and traverses only cause, firstFailedParticipant and participantFailures, so no added key can enter getControlPlaneErrorMessage, getControlPlaneErrorCode, getControlPlaneRetryAfterMs, isRetryableControlPlaneError or deriveAuthoritativeRepairCauseChain; (3) no test under test/admin or test/diagnostics deep-compares or key-counts the normalized participant, so no pre-existing assertion is weakened; (4) downstream the object is passed on BY REFERENCE (admin-service-discovery-repair-methods.js builds outcome.firstFailedParticipant and hands the same object to the repair result, the deferral record and the failure log line), and the only consumer that reads it, hasParticipantFailureRepairCause in admin-control-snapshot-repair-diagnostics.js, tests object-ness alone. Pinned by 'the admin repair summary carries the cause and decides nothing on it' in test/query/readiness-routing-denial-observability.test.js, which asserts the cause reaches the summary AND that a failure with the field produces a summary identical in every other key - cause chain, error code, retry budget, backpressure - to the same failure without it, and that an absent cause reports null rather than a guess. Blast radius: the field becomes visible on the admin authoritative-repair diagnostics surface, which is operator-facing, alongside the existing additive diagnostics causeChain and localQueryTransport.

Attempt 4, repairing the two blocking residuals of round 2. B2-residual: buildCaughtQueryExecutionFailure (src/query/sql-query-engine.js) re-projects a caught error into the caller-facing failure through an explicit key list and dropped the cause; it now reads it with readRoutingDenialCause and carries it, and readRoutingDenialCause in query-execution-budget.js was widened to read failedPartitions as well as participantFailures so a summary-shaped error is not blind. The census was re-keyed from names to CONSTRUCTION SHAPE (brace-matched function bodies over src/query plus the engine file; a body qualifies when it re-projects a failure it was handed and names at least four of fourteen failure-shape keys) and pinned at exactly nine constructors, which found a second dropping site, buildPartitionCallbackReadFailureResult in sql-query-engine-lifecycle-and-callback-dispatch.js. The transaction witness no longer stands a bare prototype up: createFrozenReadinessEngine in the rig builds a real SQLQueryEngine over a frozen readiness service and a message-router double, and the test drives real executeQuery BEGIN/UPDATE/ROLLBACK for both causes. B5-residual: the recorder's emit now resolves owner.service.logger INSIDE the try, so a throwing info getter, a throwing logger getter and a Proxy logger are counted as dropped lines like any other refusal, and an async sink that rejects gets a no-op rejection handler attached inside the guard with nothing awaited and no ordering change (the pattern main uses in admin-control-snapshot-stale-watermark-record.js). All six hostile sink shapes are now driven by the decisions-unchanged receipt and asserted to give identical served answers, identical build counts and identical queue state to a sink that works. Also: R8 pinned to an exact equality so a refusedSince that reset on every refusal would fail; the admin repair normalizer carries the cause as a pure additive pass-through and is pinned; four findings recorded (census method and its blind spots, buildControlPlaneMutationDeferredFailure, the no-single-constructor structural finding, and the admin site decision).

round 3 REJECT (1 blocking, on the error-cause clause again; no changed decision - all four differentials re-run against a git archive of the seal, 0 divergences, pinned oracle digests re-measured and matching). Both round-2 residuals are closed: BEGIN/UPDATE through executeQuery now carries the cause (absent case byte-identical to the seal over 17 error shapes; the new key reaches neither the admin websocket client nor the PostgreSQL wire), and 12 hostile logger shapes incl. thenables and a revoked Proxy are identical to the seal with 0 unhandled rejections. The victim's heartbeat path still carries the cause end to end.
